dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:2001.text: To preside over. Formed from 攴, with 典 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2002.text: To count or enumerate. Formed from 攴, with 麗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2003.text: To calculate. Formed from 攴, with 婁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2004.text: To repeatedly fold, forge and refine iron in making steel. Formed from 攴 and 湅.

shuowen:2005.text: Diligent and intent. Formed from 攴, with 子 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Diligent without slackening.”

shuowen:2006.text: To divide or distribute. Formed from 攴, with 分 indicating the sound. The Documents quotation writes a form that corresponds to 頒 in later editions. Also pronounced like 彬. [The quoted sentence requires textual collation before translation.]

shuowen:2007.text: To fend off, restrain or defend against something. Formed from 攴, with 旱 indicating the sound. The Documents quotation uses this character for later 扞, “protect or defend me in difficulties.” [The received quotation needs collation.]

shuowen:2008.text: To undertake some ordering. Formed from 攴, with 豈 indicating the sound. Read like 豤.

shuowen:2009.text: To level and prepare high ground so that one can look far away. Formed from 攴, with 尚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2010.text: To put in order. Formed from 攴, with 伸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2011.text: To change. Formed from 攴 and 己. Li Yangbing says: “When oneself has a fault, striking it brings reform.”

shuowen:2012.text: To change. Formed from 攴, with 䜌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2013.text: To change. Formed from 攴, with 丙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2014.text: To admonish. Spading the ground is also called 敕. Formed from 攴, with 束 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2015.text: To direct or employ. Formed from 攴, with abbreviated 𦔮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2016.text: To gather in. Formed from 攴, with 僉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2017.text: To select. Formed from 攴, with 𥹄 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Select and prepare your armor and helmets.”

shuowen:2018.text: To tie and join. Formed from 攴, with 喬 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Attach cords to your shields.” Read like 矯.

shuowen:2019.text: To join and assemble. Formed from 攴 and 合; 合 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:2020.text: To arrange in ranks. Formed from 攴, with 陳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2021.text: An adversary. Formed from 攴, with 啻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2022.text: To stop or prevent. Formed from 攴, with 求 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2023.text: To take by force. The Book of Zhou says: “Robbing, seizing, falsely claiming and plundering.” Formed from 攴, with 兌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2024.text: To slacken or release. Formed from 攴, with 睪 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Wear it without wearying.” 斁 means to tire of something. Another explanation: to end.

shuowen:2025.text: To set aside or release. Formed from 攴, with 赤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2026.text: The gentle, orderly flow of water. Formed from 攴 and 人, with a reduced water element.

shuowen:2027.text: To soothe. Formed from 攴, with 亾 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 撫.

shuowen:2028.text: To soothe. Formed from 攴, with 米 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Still unable to secure the duke's achievements.” Read like 弭.

shuowen:2029.text: To insult. Formed from 攴 and 易; 易 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:2030.text: To oppose or twist. Formed from 攴, with 韋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2031.text: Anger; to rebuke. Another explanation: to challenge with “who goes there?” Formed from 攴, with 𦎫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2032.text: To band together and encroach. Formed from 攴 and 羣; 羣 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:2033.text: To destroy. Formed from 攴 and 貝. Both 敗 and 賊 contain 貝, combining their components' meanings.

shuowen:2034.text: To trouble or vex. Formed from 攴 and 𤔔; 𤔔 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:2035.text: Violence. Formed from 攴 and 完.

shuowen:2036.text: To pierce. Formed from 攴, with 蚩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2037.text: To close. Formed from 攴, with 度 indicating the sound. Read like 杜.

shuowen:2038.text: To block up. Formed from 攴, with 念 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Fill your pits.”

shuowen:2039.text: To finish completely. Formed from 攴, with 畢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2040.text: To capture. Formed from 攴, with 丩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2041.text: To beat a drum. Formed from 攴 and 壴; 壴 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:2042.text: To strike. Formed from 攴, with 丂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2043.text: To strike. Formed from 攴, with 句 indicating the sound. Read like 扣.

shuowen:2044.text: To strike or attack. Formed from 攴, with 工 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2045.text: To strike or hit sideways, for example by swinging or throwing a stick. Formed from 攴, with 高 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2046.text: To strike. Formed from 攴, with 豖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2047.text: To release. Formed from 攴, with 㞷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2048.text: To split. Formed from 攴 and 厂. 厂 has a splitting nature; ripe, flavorful fruit also splits, hence called 𠩺. 未 indicates the sound. [The explanation involving 厂 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2049.text: The punishment of removing the genitals. Formed from 攴, with 蜀 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Foot amputation, nose-cutting, castration and tattooing.”

shuowen:2050.text: To venture recklessly. Formed from 攴, with 昬 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “Recklessly unafraid of death.”

shuowen:2051.text: To prohibit. Another explanation: the musical instrument 椌楬, shaped like a wooden tiger. Formed from 攴, with 吾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2052.text: To grind and work. Formed from 攴, with 果 indicating the sound. Shun's younger sister was named 㪙首.

shuowen:2053.text: To hold. Formed from 攴, with 金 indicating the sound. Read like 琴.

shuowen:2054.text: To abandon. Formed from 攴, with 𠷎 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou uses it for 討. The Odes says: “Do not abandon me.”

shuowen:2055.text: To level fields. Formed from 攴 and 田. The Book of Zhou says: “Level your fields.”

shuowen:2056.text: 㱾改, a large 剛卯 amulet for driving away ghosts and spirits. Formed from 攴, with 巳 indicating the sound. Read like 巳.

shuowen:2057.text: Sequence or order. Formed from 攴, with 余 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2058.text: To destroy. Formed from 攴, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2059.text: To destroy, 㪏. Formed from 攴, with 兒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2060.text: A person tending cattle. Formed from 攴 and 牛. The Odes says: “The herdsman dreamed.”

shuowen:2061.text: To strike a horse. Formed from 攴, with 朿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2062.text: To pound lightly. Formed from 攴, with 算 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2063.text: To work fields, glossed 䚫田. Formed from 攴, with 堯 indicating the sound. [The action expressed by the rare gloss 䚫 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2064.text: What superiors impart and inferiors imitate. Formed from 攴 and 孝. All characters in the 教 category are formed from 教.

shuowen:2065.text: To awaken to understanding. Formed from 教 and 冂; 冂 indicates still being unenlightened. 𦥑 indicates the sound.

shuowen:2066.text: To scorch and crack a tortoise shell. It depicts heating a tortoise shell. Another explanation: it depicts vertical and horizontal divination cracks. All characters in the 卜 category are formed from 卜.

shuowen:2067.text: To divine with stalks. Formed from 卜, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2068.text: To divine in order to resolve doubts. Formed from 口 and 卜. Pronounced the same as 稽. The Documents says: “卟 doubts.”

shuowen:2069.text: To inquire by divination. Formed from 卜, with 貝 as an offering. Another explanation: abbreviated 鼎 indicates the sound. Jing Fang's explanation.

shuowen:2070.text: The upper body of a hexagram in the Changes. The Book of Shang says: “The divination says 𠧩.” Formed from 卜, with 每 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2071.text: To inspect cracks and inquire. Formed from 卜 and 口.

shuowen:2072.text: To inquire by divination. Formed from 卜, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2073.text: Cracks from heating a tortoise shell. Formed from 卜; 兆 is pictographic.

shuowen:2074.text: Capable of being put into practice. Formed from 卜 and 中. Wei Hong's explanation. All characters in the 用 category are formed from 用.

shuowen:2075.text: An honorific designation for a man. Formed from 用 and 父; 父 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:2076.text: To use. Formed from 用 and 庚; 庚 means to manage affairs. The Changes says: “Three days before geng.”

shuowen:2077.text: To provide or possess. Formed from 用 and abbreviated 茍.

shuowen:2078.text: What one wishes for. Formed from 用, with abbreviated 寕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2079.text: To cross. It depicts the crossing ends of the six lines of the Changes. All characters in the 爻 category are formed from 爻.

shuowen:2080.text: A fence. Formed from 爻 and 林. The Odes says: “Buzzing blue flies alight on the fence.”

shuowen:2081.text: Two 爻. All characters in the 㸚 category are formed from 㸚.

shuowen:2082.text: 麗爾: like elaborate beauty. Formed from 冂 and 㸚, its openings 㸚; 尒 indicates the sound. This shares the underlying idea of 爽. [The clause about the openings is uncertain.]

shuowen:2083.text: Bright. Formed from 㸚 and 大.

shuowen:2084.text: To raise the eyes to direct someone. Formed from 攴 and 目. All characters in the 𡕥 category are formed from 𡕥. Read like 𩖶.

shuowen:2085.text: To seek earnestly. Formed from 𡕥, with 人 above 穴. The Book of Shang says: “Gaozong dreamed of finding Yue; he made the hundred officers search earnestly and found him at Fuyan.” 巗 means a cave.

shuowen:2086.text: To look with lowered eyes. Formed from 𡕥, with 門 indicating the sound. Hu county in Hongnong has a 䦩 township; Xiping in Runan has a 䦩 station.

shuowen:2087.text: To look broadly or intently. Formed from 大 and 𡕥. Read like 齤.

shuowen:2088.text: A human eye. A pictograph, with a doubled pupil. All characters in the 目 category are formed from 目.

shuowen:2089.text: The eye. Formed from 目, with 𥃩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2090.text: A newborn infant whose eyes glance sideways. Formed from 目, with 瞏 indicating the sound. [The precise eye condition is uncertain.]

shuowen:2091.text: Eyes without a steady focus. Formed from 目, with 玄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2092.text: The frame or socket of the eye. Formed from 目, with 此 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2093.text: Hairs at the edge of the eye. Formed from 目, with 夾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2094.text: The dark pupil of the eye. Formed from 目, with 縣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2095.text: The essence of the eye's pupil. Formed from 目, with 喜 indicating the sound. Read like 禧.

shuowen:2096.text: A thin, closely fitted covering at the eye's edge. Formed from 目, with 𦤝 indicating the sound. [The descriptive 宀宀 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2097.text: Large eyes. Formed from 目, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2098.text: Large eyes. Formed from 目, with 臤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2099.text: Large eyes. Formed from 目, with 旱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2100.text: Large eyes. Formed from 目, with 爰 indicating the sound.
